transcript.text: “Won’t come on” can mean a few different things. The common simple one is the clock/timer being left in AUTO after a power interruption; if it is completely dead, the cooker isolator or circuit supply is more likely. A heating or control fault comes later once those are ruled out. 1. If it is electric and completely dead, check the cooker isolator switch is on and that no circuit breaker/RCD has tripped. Do not remove any panels or touch wiring. If a breaker trips again, leave the oven isolated and arrange an engineer. 2. If the clock/display is working, look for a flashing time or an AUTO/A symbol. Set the clock and change the timer to the MANUAL/hand symbol, then try an oven function again. This often restores operation and does not mean a part has failed. Is the clock/display lit or is the oven completely dead, and is it an electric or gas oven?
electric, Neff. display is lit but flashing 0.00 and a little symbol. there was a power cut last night

This is most likely the clock/timer having reset into automatic operation after the power cut, rather than an oven fault. A flashing 0.00 and small symbol are typical of that state, and many Neff ovens will not heat until the time is set and the timer is returned to manual. 1. Use the clock/timer buttons to set the current time. Usually you press or hold the clock button, then adjust with +/– or the dial.
2. Cancel any AUTO/A or cooking-duration setting until the hand/manual symbol is displayed. If the small symbol is a hand, that is normally the correct manual setting.
3. Leave the cooker switched on at the wall, then select an oven function and temperature and try it again. Do not switch it off at the wall as a reset: that can simply put the timer back to 0.00/AUTO. If it still will not heat after the clock is set and manual operation is selected, the next possibilities are the programmer controls or an oven heating/control fault rather than the power supply.
how do i set the clock though, i dont have the manual

On Neff ovens the exact method varies by the control panel, but do this first with the cooker left switched on: 1. Press the button with a clock symbol once. If the digits start flashing, adjust the time using the +/− buttons, or turn the nearby rotary dial.
2. Press the clock button again to save it, or wait a few seconds for it to stop flashing.
3. If the little symbol is an “A” or a saucepan/arrow symbol, press the button with a hand symbol, or press and hold the clock/timer button for a few seconds, until AUTO disappears and/or a hand appears.
4. Then select an oven function and temperature and try it. Avoid turning the cooker off at the wall while doing this, as the clock will reset to 0.00 again. If you tell me whether the controls are clock and +/− buttons, or a dial, I can give the right button sequence; a photo of the panel is ideal.
ok tried it, set the time and it came on and heated. thanks

That suggests it was only the clock/timer reset after the power cut, not an oven fault. If there is another power cut, set the time again and return the timer to manual before using the oven. Is there anything else you need help with?
